card.name: Chopi (Choobi)
card.tagline: Gulf-style Iranian line dance led by a handkerchief-waving leader
card.profile: In the Iranian context, 'chopi'/'choobi' denotes a Bandari/Khaleeji-style group line dance of southern Iran, related to the broader Gulf (khaleeji) and stick-dance traditions. The word is cognate with the Lori/Lorestan collective dance 'Chopi,' in which a leader called the sarchoopi stands at the front waving one or two colored handkerchiefs while the others hold hands and synchronize their steps to a solo singer accompanied by sorna and kamancheh (orienttrips.com). It is also tied to choob/choub-bazi ('stick play'), a chain or social dance found across Iran (Choub bazi, Wikipedia).
card.insight: The root 'chop/choob' (stick/wood) links these Gulf and Lori forms to the trans-national Iraqi Chobi/Choubi and the Kurdish copi, all sharing the same etymology and line-dance character (Choub bazi, Wikipedia).
card.image_significance: The Lur handkerchief-led chain. A representative image shows a line or row formation, often with canes, swords or flowing veils — Lorestan (Lur), Iran.
